purpose: Record positive and negative performance effects; preserve intermediate measurements, including regressions corrected during implementation.

method.frequency_control: Uncontrolled boost/governor; shared machine. Paired sampling reduces drift, but intervals do not model systematic host interference.
method.compiler: rustc opt-level=2 debuginfo=0, identical cached native dependencies and newly built baseline support crates on both sides
method.candidate_workload: Existing EPUB benchmark source unchanged; CSS fixtures replaced with 64 classes using counter-reset, counter-increment, content:counter(), and :has(p). Forms valid and rendered equivalently in both builds.
method.ci_method: 5000 bootstrap resamples of paired percentage changes; deterministic seed 173, median, 2.5/97.5 percentiles; no multiple-comparison adjustment. Diagnostic evidence, not a universal performance claim.

method.fallback_workload: Same candidate CSS plus flex-basis:min-content and z-index:calc(3 - 2). Baseline ignores these declarations; the changed build applies them. This measures added feature cost, not equivalent-output regression.
method.combined_metric: all_samples sums the five sample medians per invocation; it is cumulative sample time, not a simultaneous page or peak.

interpretation: Positive percentage changes mean slower. All point changes and bootstrap ranges are retained, including inconclusive positive results.

Two final measured slowdowns have entirely positive bootstrap ranges: normalization retry and the reference EPUB sample with uncached author-program preparation. These are small sampled regressions, not universal engine slowdown estimates.
Equivalent content/counter workload improves about 9% without author-program reuse and 14% with reuse after eligibility caching.
Fallback workloads add intrinsic flex-basis and numeric z-index that the baseline ignored. Their timings include additional feature work and are not equivalent-output regressions.
The final fallback-cold point estimate is positive, but its interval crosses zero. This does not establish zero overhead.
CPU boost/frequency was uncontrolled on a shared machine. Confidence intervals are diagnostic bootstrap ranges and have no multiple-comparison correction.
Cold means clearing the author style-program cache; default CSS and machine caches have been warmed.
Existing benchmark Rust sources were used unchanged. Only CSS fixture data differs for the two dedicated workloads.
